steps: MRI with contrast; refer neuro-oncology / neurosurgery.
Dexamethasone for symptomatic vasogenic oedema (with PPI cover).
Antiepileptics only if seizures have occurred (not routine prophylaxis).
Definitive therapy (surgery, radiotherapy, chemotherapy) is tumour-specific via MDT.

drugRefs.dose: 10 mg loading, then 4 mg every 6 hours (titrate to lowest effective dose)
drugRefs.why: Reduces symptomatic vasogenic oedema and raised intracranial pressure. Withhold if primary CNS lymphoma is suspected until biopsy, as steroids can render tissue non-diagnostic.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Primary and Metastatic Tumors of the Nervous System
EANO Guidelines on Diagnosis and Treatment of Gliomas
NICE NG99 — Brain Tumours (Primary) and Brain Metastases in Adults

recommendations.regimenLabel: Seizure control (only if a seizure has occurred)

drugRefs.dose: 500 mg twice daily, titrate to response
drugRefs.why: For patients who have had a tumour-related seizure. Prophylactic antiepileptics have no role in patients who have never seized (except sometimes perioperatively).

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Primary and Metastatic Tumors of the Nervous System
NICE NG99 — Brain Tumours (Primary) and Brain Metastases in Adults

decision.label: Dexamethasone for oedema; urgent neuro referral

confirm: Progressive headache (worse on waking/Valsalva), focal signs, new seizures, or papilloedema. MRI brain with contrast.
